mentl/6be966e:
The sugar set was measured at 44 names by scanning quoted literals and
banked honestly as a lower bound: a name assembled by splicing a
fold_sig would be invisible to that scan. So the splices were enumerated
instead of assumed. All 55 across the lowering, the backend and infer
are compiler-synthesized — __hstate_{h}, __fb_prev_{h},
__fanout_spawn_{i}_{h}, lambda_{n}, compose_{side}_{h},
hash_{fold_sig}, tuple_{int_to_str(h)} — naming wasm locals, globals and
generated functions the compiler emits itself, never a call into lib.
Of forty distinct spliced prefixes only tuple_ shares a namespace with a
prelude decl, and its splice produces tuple_1234, never tuple_get. The
literal scan sees the whole vocabulary, so the demand-link's seed is
complete.

verify now holds desugar_vocabulary: 43 exact — 44 minus the
str_literal_5 relic deleted at the previous pin. The reason is not
hygiene: when that set changes, the demand-link's seed must change with
it, and nothing else in the repo would say so.

Two red tests refuted the gate's first comment, which had claimed it
catches a prelude rename breaking a desugar path. Renaming list_to_flat
in lib aborted verify long before the check ran, because the wheel's own
source calls it and that break is already loud. Corrupting one
"list_to_flat" literal left the count at 43, because this is set
membership and the name appears more than once. What it does catch was
then seen red properly: a new prelude name entering the vocabulary moved
43 to 44 and refused. The comment and the failure message now claim
exactly that and no more.

The baseline value was written by arithmetic and only then measured. It
agreed, but the order was wrong.

first lesson rides along: an unnarrated head is a working step, so a

mentl/6bc19ba:
Productive-under-error refinement to the canonical name projection
(commit 851a517). Adds two structural checks before reading the LFn
record's name field:

  1. Heap-base guard: pointer < HEAP_BASE → synth from pointer.
     Prevents emit_str on data-segment addresses.

  2. Tag-equality guard: tag_of(r) != 350 → synth from pointer.
     Prevents reading record_get(r, 0) on a non-LFn record.

When upstream lower emits a malformed LMakeClosure whose fn-field is
a non-LFn payload (string-literal pointer, sentinel, mis-tagged
record), the projection falls back to the pointer-derived synth and
lets dedup handle the rest. Drift "imperative subsystem" remains
refused: the projection IS the cursor reading the graph; what it
finds is what it returns.

Empirical: same fn count + zero empty-name; the residual single
wat2wasm error (Hβ.first-light.emit-string-literal-pointer-leak) is
distinct — the LFn record itself is well-formed (tag 350) but its
name field holds a string-literal pointer; investigation is at the
lower-side now (where $lowfn_make's name argument originates).
mentl/6b2e5ac:
Two upstream bugs whose symptom was emit_binop_i32 mistranslating Mul→Add
and every string literal data segment being emitted with a length header
but zero payload bytes. Both root causes were one-liners above the emitter.

1. std/compiler/lower.lux — lower_pat mapped PLit(e) to LPLit(LUnit),
   unconditionally throwing away the literal value. Every match-on-literal
   collapsed to match-on-unit, and emit_match_arms' LPLit arm always fired
   the first body regardless of the scrutinee. That's why the bootstrap's
   emit_binop_i32("Mul") returned "    i32.add" — it returned the first
   arm's body no matter the op. Fix: unwrap the parser's S(expr,line,col)
   span wrapper via a helper (Lux parser doesn't accept nested let/match
   inside a match arm body) and preserve the literal via lit_expr_to_lval.

2. std/runtime/memory.lux — byte_at and byte_len were declared via
   env_extend in ty.lux, which means collect_top_names never found them
   and is_global returned false. The closure-capture detector then pulled
   them into upvals, and emit_call_expr emitted a call_indirect through
   a closure slot that was never initialized. Every emit_escape_wat_bytes
   iteration called garbage, writing zero bytes per string. Symmetric
   fix: add byte_at and byte_len to the Memory effect declaration, so
   EffectDeclStmt puts them in globals where they belong. Callers in
   wasm_collect.lux now annotate `with WasmOut, Memory`.

3. std/backend/wasm_construct.lux — emit_match_arms had LPLit(_) emit
   the body unconditionally (pre-existing dead code since LPLit never
   carried useful values). Now properly compares $__match against the
   literal via i32.eq for Int/Bool or call $str_eq for String, then
   branches.

4. std/backend/wasm_collect.lux — visit_pat now collects LPLit string
   literals into the strings list so find_string_offset can resolve them
   when emit_match_arm_lit generates `call $str_eq`.

5. std/compiler/lower_print.lux — enhanced to show literal patterns,

sonido/6bf2348:
Replace fixed 480×380 window with host-negotiated resize. PendingResize
packs width/height into AtomicU64 — host writes via set_size(), baseview
handler reads in on_frame() and calls window.resize(). Lock-free,
single-word atomic, no torn reads.

CLAP resize protocol fully implemented:
- can_resize() → true
- get_resize_hints() → free resize, no aspect ratio constraint
- adjust_size() → clamp to 320×240 min, 1920×1080 max
- set_size() → write to atomic channel
- get_size() → read current size from atomic

fixed-size simplification.
clob/6bca41e:
The bridge that makes a trained core measurable by the dynamics
instrument -- and the first look at whether lambda1 climbs as the core
learns. The learning lives in the f32 latents (the naive ternary
projection loses most of it), so the payoff is measurable on the latent
core, not on a ternary CoreModel; this measures the latent core
directly rather than bridging through the lossy projection.

DenseModel gains the stateful API CoreModel already had -- reset_state,
decode_step (forward_window's per-token forward without the tape),
export_state/import_state -- so it can be stepped one token at a time
and snapshotted. decode_step_matches_forward_window_logits pins it to
the gradient-checked forward token-for-token; dense_state_snapshot_
roundtrips proves the snapshot is complete. DenseModelTwin implements
the same TwinSystem the Lyapunov estimator already drives, so no new
estimation code. clob regime gains --dense <artifact> (and --ternary to
measure the effective-ternary projection); the estimate/report tail is
now generic over the twin type and shared with the CoreModel path.

First measurement, mini dense core on eval_corpus.txt (byte level),
before vs after training -- same architecture, so the comparison is
valid (this is NOT the d=128 ternary core that measured -1.23):

  core           NLL(/unigram 3.02)   lambda1   horizon
  random init    --                   -0.398    2.5 tok
  2500 steps     1.36                 -0.163    6.1 tok
  6000 steps     0.73                 -0.112    8.9 tok

As capability rises, lambda1 rises monotonically toward zero and the
state-memory horizon grows 3.6x. That is Bet 7's mechanism, observed:
the core leaves deep contraction as it learns to hold context. A single
before/after/mid trajectory is a first data point, not the full Bet 7
test (>=5 checkpoints + a rank correlation on a real corpus), which the
instrument now enables. 118 tests pass.
perennials/6b57c77:
Everything she writes is device-local storage, and the one real way to lose
it is the browser reclaiming space — iOS clears a tab's storage after about a
week of not visiting a site that is not on the home screen, which is exactly
how a seasonal guide gets used. So Field notes gains a quiet install hint
above the backup panel: on iOS it names the Add-to-Home-Screen gesture, on a
browser that offers a prompt it shows an Install button, and it says nothing
at all once the app is standalone or where nothing can be installed. Installing
wins persistent storage and exempts her from that sweep; the backup below is
still the floor under everything.

Docs catch up with the work. The README gains a "Your data" section: where her
data lives, that a deploy or service-worker update never touches it (autoUpdate
reloads once, no hard refresh, Workbox only clears its own caches), and how to
guard against eviction. The data section lists her as the fourth source. CLAUDE.md
records the same, plus the rule that keeps it true: add optional fields, never
rename a store key without a migration, because that is the only way code can
lose her data. The test list and the "eight stores" count (nine now, with
latitude) are brought current.
